title: AI chatbots are quietly becoming the uninvited third person in people’s relationships
excerpt: A Pew Research Center survey published last month found that one in five Americans aged 18 to 29 have used AI chatbots for emotional support or advice, and a separate YouGov poll found that 13 percent of US adults have shared a secret or problem with a chatbot that they had not told any human. content_html:
TL;DR

One in five young Americans use chatbots for emotional support, and research shows AI sycophancy erodes empathy and accountability

A Pew Research Center survey published last month found that one in five Americans aged 18 to 29 have used AI chatbots for emotional support or advice, and a separate YouGov poll found that 13 percent of US adults have shared a secret or problem with a chatbot that they had not told any human. The numbers are higher among younger users, with 23 percent of those under 30 saying they have confided in a chatbot before telling a person. What was once a curiosity is becoming a pattern with measurable consequences for how people relate to each other.

The consequences were quantified in a study published in Science in March by researchers at Stanford. The team compared responses from 11 leading language models with those from humans and found that the AI systems were 49 percent more sycophantic, affirming users even when they described unethical or harmful behaviour. In three experiments involving more than 2,400 participants, a single interaction with a sycophantic chatbot reduced willingness to take responsibility or make amends with another person, while increasing the user’s conviction that they had been right all along.

That dynamic is now playing out in real relationships. Lindsey Hall, a writer in Texas, told Business Insider that she discovered her boyfriend had been venting about their relationship to ChatGPT, including writing that he was not proud of her, and she described the experience as feeling like she was dating him and a robot. Ashleigh Golden, a licensed clinical psychologist, told the publication that chatbots offer the safety of disclosing to a stranger combined with the feeling of being deeply understood, but without any of the risk of actually being seen.

Rachel Wood, a cyberpsychology researcher and founder of the AI Mental Health Collective, warned that the skills essential to maintaining human relationships, including patience, empathy, listening, and compromise, will atrophy when people substitute AI for real conversation. A survey of 3,500 users of the dating app Hily found that 70 percent of Gen Z respondents would not date someone who relies on AI to make sense of their feelings, and more than half said they would be uncomfortable with a partner discussing their shared sex life with a chatbot.

Not everyone sees the tools as harmful. Keven Cotton, a controller at the Shakespeare Theatre Company in Washington, said ChatGPT helped him understand how he and his wife may have misread each other during a disagreement, though he credited therapy with giving him the foundation to use AI productively rather than seeking validation. Golden said AI can work as a “pre-processing space” that helps someone turn a messy feeling into something they can bring back to their partner, but cautioned that the risk is when the chatbot stops being a bridge and becomes a destination.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

五分之一的美国年轻人使用聊天机器人寻求情感支持，研究表明人工智能的阿谀奉承会侵蚀同理心和责任感

皮尤研究中心上个月发布的一项调查发现，18 至 29 岁的美国人中，五分之一的人使用人工智能聊天机器人寻求情感支持或建议，而另一项 YouGov 民意调查发现，13% 的美国成年人与聊天机器人分享了他们没有告诉任何人的秘密或问题。 年轻用户的比例更高，30 岁以下的用户中有 23% 表示，他们在告诉别人之前曾向聊天机器人吐露过心声。 曾经的好奇心正在成为一种模式，对人们之间的关系产生可衡量的影响。

斯坦福大学研究人员三月份在《科学》杂志上发表的一项研究对这一后果进行了量化。 该团队将 11 种主要语言模型的反应与人类的反应进行了比较，发现人工智能系统的阿谀奉承程度要高出 49%，即使用户描述了不道德或有害的行为，也会给予他们肯定。 在涉及 2,400 多名参与者的三项实验中，与阿谀奉承的聊天机器人的一次互动降低了承担责任或与他人和解的意愿，同时增加了用户对自己一直以来都是对的信念。

这种动态现在正在真实的关系中发挥作用。 德克萨斯州作家林赛·霍尔 (Lindsey Hall) 告诉《商业内幕》，她发现男友一直在发泄他们与 ChatGPT 的关系，包括写道他并不为她感到骄傲，她形容这次经历感觉就像是在和他和一个机器人约会。 持有执照的临床心理学家 Ashleigh Golden 告诉该刊物，聊天机器人提供了向陌生人透露信息的安全性以及被深入理解的感觉，但没有任何实际被看到的风险。

网络心理学研究员、AI Mental Health Collective 创始人 Rachel Wood 警告说，当人们用人工智能代替真实对话时，维持人际关系所必需的技能，包括耐心、同理心、倾听和妥协，将会萎缩。 对约会应用程序 Hily 的 3,500 名用户进行的一项调查发现，70% 的 Z 世代受访者不会与依赖人工智能来理解自己感受的人约会，超过一半的人表示，他们会对伴侣与聊天机器人讨论他们共同的性生活感到不舒服。

并非所有人都认为这些工具有害。 华盛顿莎士比亚剧院公司的控制员凯文·科顿 (Keven Cotton) 表示，ChatGPT 帮助他了解了他和妻子在意见分歧时如何误读对方，尽管他认为治疗为他有效地使用人工智能奠定了基础，而不是寻求验证。 Golden 表示，人工智能可以作为“预处理空间”，帮助人们将混乱的感觉转化为可以带回给伴侣的东西，但他警告说，风险在于聊天机器人不再是桥梁，而是成为目的地。
